messages.content: if i say my brother had the key yesterday, does that say he has it now?
no. had the key yesterday is about yesterday. he may still have it, or he may have given it to someone else.
now i say he has the key.
then you are giving the information that he has it now.
can both sentences be true?
yes. he could have had it yesterday and still have it now.
what if he gave it to me this morning?
then he had it yesterday, but you have it now, if you have kept it after he gave it to you.
i did keep it. make that one sentence.
my brother had the key yesterday, but i have it now.
why not say he never had it?
because you gave a time when he did have it. a change in who has it now does not change the fact about yesterday.
make that explanation shorter.
he had it yesterday. your having it now does not make yesterday different.
only give the sentence with both people again.
my brother had the key yesterday, but i have it now.
write a story about a child asking when lunch is ready and getting an answer about what the meal is. she should ask again in a kind way.

a child came into the kitchen and asked when lunch would be ready. her father said that he was making rice and vegetables. she liked the sound of the meal, but still did not know whether she had time to finish a page of her book. she said she liked that meal, then asked whether she had a few minutes before the food was ready. he looked at the pot and said she had about five minutes. she returned to her book and finished the page. the first answer had given useful information, but it was not the information she needed for her choice.
what did she ask first?
she asked when lunch would be ready.
what did the first answer tell her instead?
it told her what her father was making.
why did she need the time?
she wanted to know whether she could finish a page before eating.
write her next question in her own voice.
that sounds good. do i have a few minutes to finish my page before lunch is ready?
make that question shorter.
do i have a few minutes to finish my page before lunch?
finish with her coming back when called.
she put the book down when her father called and came to the table. she could tell him what happened on the page while they ate.
i sent my friend two questions: are you free tomorrow, and do you want to go to the park. they only said yes. can i know which question they answered?
not for sure. yes might answer both, but it could also answer just one. you can ask to make the plan clear.
write that question without making it sound like they did something wrong.
do you mean you are free tomorrow and would like to go to the park?
what if they only mean they want to go, but are not free tomorrow?
then you still need another day. your friend may want to go without being free tomorrow.
can i ask one question at a time to make it easy?
yes. you could ask first whether they are free tomorrow, then ask about the park after you know the day works.
make that explanation shorter.
yes. one question at a time can help make each answer clear.
now just give the question about tomorrow.
are you free tomorrow?
they answer no. should i still ask what time tomorrow?
not for that plan. if they are not free tomorrow, ask about another day instead.
only give that next question.
would another day work for you?
give me examples with right and write.
you are right about the time. please write the time on the page.
can right also tell someone which way to go?
yes. turn right at the school is about which way to go. you are right is about being correct.
use right and write in one sentence about a map.
please write turn right on the map near the school.
why not use write for the way to go?
write is about putting words on a page or screen. right can tell someone which way to turn or that an answer is correct.
make that explanation shorter.
write is for putting words down. right can be a way to turn or a word for correct.
if someone says is this the right word, are they asking which side it is on?
usually not. they are asking whether the word is correct for what they mean.
now only give a request about writing a name.
please write your name here.
can i say write it on the right side?
yes. write is about putting it down, and right is about the side.
i want to ask my friend to do something that does not cost money. do not say they have no money. this is my choice for today.
you could say: i would like to do something free today. would you like to go for a walk with me?
what if i do not want to choose what we do yet?
i would like to do something free today. do you have an idea?
can you keep that from being a rule for every day?
yes. today already makes the request about this day. you can also say for this afternoon if that is the time you mean.
use this afternoon.
i would like to do something free this afternoon. do you have an idea?
why not say we have no money?
because you did not give that as a fact about either of you. you can have money and still choose not to spend it today.
only give that last idea.
you can have money and still choose not to spend it today.
now only give the walking question.
would you like to go for a walk with me this afternoon?
what happened to the free part?
the walk is what you chose to ask about. if you want the cost choice clear too, add that you would like something free.
write a story about a person who wants to show someone around a house on their first visit. the person should not ask do you remember where everything is.

a woman came to visit her friend for the first time. after he showed her the kitchen and the room where she could sleep, he began to ask whether she remembered the house. then he stopped and said he should ask what she still needed to know. she asked which door went to the bathroom and where to put her things. he showed her those places without going through the whole house again. later, she could find the kitchen herself but asked about another room. one visit had given her some information, not every detail at once.
why would do you remember where everything is not be a useful first question?
she had never visited before. she needed information, not a test of a place she already knew.
explain that more simply.
it would ask her to remember something she had not known before the visit.
what was a better question?
what would you like me to show you before you put your things away?
why did he not need to explain every room again?
she asked for specific places. answering those questions could help without giving the whole explanation again.
finish with her asking about one place she still needs.
she found the kitchen in the morning, then asked where they kept cups. he showed her the shelf and let her choose one.
i saw a flower on my walk and did not take a picture. i just looked for a while.
what made you want to stop and look?
the color. i do not know the flower name, but i liked seeing its color near the wall.
you saw something you liked without having to know its name first.
make that a little shorter.
you could enjoy it without knowing its name.
can i tell someone about it without knowing the specific flower?
yes. you can tell someone its color, where it was, or what you liked. not knowing the name does not mean you have no details to share.
make that explanation shorter.
you can tell them the details you know without giving a name.
write one sentence using only what i gave.
i stopped on my walk to look at a flower because i liked its color near the wall.
does that say what color it was?
no. you have not given the color itself.
now make it blue.
i stopped on my walk to look at a blue flower near the wall.
my sister and brother read six pages together in all. can you know how many each read?
not from that alone. your sister could read some and your brother the rest, or they might read the same pages together. you need to say what happened.
make that explanation shorter.
six pages in all does not say how many each person read or whether they read the same pages.
now i say each read different pages, and my sister read four.
then your brother read two, making six different pages between them.
what if both read the same two pages too?
then we need to keep clear whether six is the number of different pages or the added reading by each person. the same pages can be part of both their reading.
say that more simply.
we need to know what six is about. is it six different pages, or six when you add what each person read?
say six different pages. my sister read four, my brother read four, and two of those were the same pages.
that can work. each read four, and two pages were read by both. there were six different pages between them.
can you know which page came first?
no. you gave how many, not the order.
only give the number of different pages again.
six.
